critical_code_review_comments: server.py phishing-sim (line 991-1001) ordering is correct — _load_scan (which raises 404 for cross-tenant) runs before the plan-check that would return 402. This is the right pattern; consider extracting a small helper `_require_pro(user)` to unify the 402 raise across the many pro-gated endpoints (attack-path, phishing-sim, etc.).

telegram_bot.py webhook silently returns {ok:true} when admin has no bot configured (lines 98-99, 104-105). Good defense in depth, but consider also 200-noop when a message has no chat_id (already handled at line 119-120). No bug — just noting the branch is unreachable for the tested admin.

emailer.py: `send_email` returns dict {ok:False,error} instead of raising; server.py:807-809 translates that to a 502. Consistent. However `send_alerts_email`/`send_scan_complete_email`/`send_blocked_login_email` fire-and-forget from server.py:120 — errors are only logged. If Resend rate-limits, users will silently lose notifications. Consider persisting failed emails in a `email_queue` for retry.
waf_bypass.py `WAF_PLAYBOOK` has entry 'Sucuri (Generic)' with empty techniques (line 105) — dead-code branch since detection returns 'Sucuri' not 'Sucuri (Generic)'. Safe to remove.

stealth.py `stealth_httpx_client` is a plain factory returning `httpx.AsyncClient` — it does NOT provide jittered inter-request delay (that's only in `StealthClient` context manager). Modules that use the factory get only header rotation, not timing evasion. Consider documenting the trade-off (or exposing a middleware/event_hook variant that adds delay).
